Published physical-quintessence fits with free curvature on DESI DR2 prefer open curvature. The bimetric aligned vacuum is not a k = +1 FRW solution on the program's zero-vacuum-energy branch: H² = −k/a² (see C51). With matter, Υ ≠ 1 for any k. Closure does not help with persistence under expansion.

Higuchi applies to de Sitter space in any slicing, including the k = +1 global slicing, so the open item 'no closed-FRW version found' is moot for de Sitter. For X today the bound holds with a margin of 2.6×10³⁰; only the early universe, where H > M_X, matters (addendum_numbers.out).

Missed prior art for a doubly compact or compact Born-reciprocal phase space: Artigas, Mielczarek and Rovelli, PRD 100, 043533 (2019), arXiv:1904.11338. Compactifying the minisuperspace phase space produces both UV and IR effects: 'the phase of re-collapse appears, preventing the universe from expanding to infinite volume'. The paper cites Born reciprocity (source l.68). This bears directly on 'how big does position space get'. Also Mielczarek and Trześniewski 2017 (1704.01934), Yargic 2020 (modular path integral on a compact phase space), and Pachoł 2024 (2409.05110: density of states in the Snyder–de Sitter and Yang models, a modern analogue of Born's eq. 9).

Missed prior art for closed momentum space and reciprocal gravity: Moffat, gr-qc/0401117 (IJGMMP 13, 1650005). Following Born, it writes a p-space line element that is 'the p-space equivalent of the FRW line element' with ζ = +1 closed and a maximum momentum. Castro, 'Born's reciprocal gravity in curved phase-spaces and the cosmological constant', Found. Phys. 42 (2012), found as an INSPIRE title only (†).

Missed prior art for duality bounding cosmic size: Tseytlin, CQG 9, 979 (1992), hep-th/9112004. In duality-symmetric closed-string cosmology on a torus, the scale factor oscillates between maximal and minimal values, and winding modes 'prevent infinite expansion'. This is a duality-based maximum size, though the space is flat and compact, not k = +1. Also Bento and Bertolami 1995 (scale-factor duality in quantum cosmology) and Barrow and Dąbrowski 1998 (Bianchi IX string cosmology).

Missed prior art on the size of a closed universe: Lehners and Quintin, PLB 850, 138488 (2024), 'A small Universe'. The no-boundary proposal favours a closed universe not much larger than the observed one. Also Kanekar, Sahni and Shtanov 2001 (closed universes cycling under V ≥ 0).

Born 1938 restricts its metrics to two limiting cases. Born writes that the metric 'is inapplicable for those phenomena in which x-space and p-space are involved simultaneously with about equal weight' (p. 293). His b is a nuclear scale, about 140 MeV/c. A state count combining the universe's 3-sphere with a momentum 3-sphere is therefore outside Born's scheme, and Born gives no support for it. The momentum-cutoff idea itself predates Born: his footnote credits Born and Rumer 1931, Wataghin 1934 and March 1937.

Born's measure covers one hemisphere of the momentum S³. A count over the full sphere would be n = 4π⁴g(ab/h)³, not 2π⁴g(ab/h)³ (symbolic_independent.out). Which one the program means should be stated.

result.overall: The quotations and transcriptions hold up. All 15 survey numbers I re-read from the arXiv LaTeX match (Planck 2018, DESI DR1 and DR2, ACT DR6, SPT-3G, Giarè et al.), as do the Born 1938 quotes, checked against page images I downloaded myself, and the FHSW, Tipler, Gialamas and bimetric sources. The arithmetic recomputes. The weak link is applicability, and it changes the answer to 'how big does position space get'. (1) The closed-side bounds are central-95% marginal edges. For a universe presumed closed, the right statistic is the bound conditional on closure, and ACT's quoted 105 Gpc is consistent with that reading. Under it, ΛCDM+K DESI DR2+CMB gives R_c > ~130 Gpc rather than 'none', and the w0waCDM+K proxy gives about 95–101 Gpc rather than 101–117. (2) w0waCDM+K is the wrong proxy for a w ≥ −1 cosine field. Published physical-quintessence-plus-curvature fits to DESI DR2 prefer an open universe at about 3σ (Akrami, Alestas and Nesseris 2025; also Dinda and Maartens; Chudaykin et al.), so in the program's own model class closure is observationally disfavoured, not merely allowed. (3) The bimetric claim that the aligned vacuum 'survives k = +1' is algebraically true but has no k = +1 solution on the program's zero-vacuum branch (H² = −k/a²). (4) Radii use H0 = 67.4 rather than each chain's own H0, a 2% effect. Of the record errors: the 93.8% wording complaint is partly upheld but overstated, since the abstract's own wording and 'both scenarios imply future collapse' cover the record's phrase. The FHSW 'not cited' claim is largely wrong because the wiki already cites it (†). The R11 citation gap is upheld; the closed-turnaround statement sits inside a [D]-tagged paragraph of the diameter note. The novelty audit's (i) conclusion (no source derives closure from reciprocity) survives an expanded INSPIRE, arXiv and web search. It missed directly relevant prior art for compact phase spaces that make the universe recollapse (Artigas, Mielczarek and Rovelli 2019; Mielczarek and Trześniewski 2017), closed momentum space after Born (Moffat), duality-bounded size (Tseytlin 1992) and small closed universes (Lehners and Quintin 2023). Not reached: C4, C27–C29, C47, C48, C59's quote, C60, C61 (arXiv rate limit); Semantic Scholar, Google Scholar and ADS were unavailable.
